refinery.busy_shift_confirmed.name: Busy shift with every station inside its band
refinery.busy_shift_confirmed.summary: A line that carried a planned product changeover on top of a full production shift and still held its target rate, with a station-by-station sweep finding nothing outside its normal band. The checks are what makes the all-clear worth reading.

pipeline.title: Busy
pipeline.text: the line has a planned changeover today: its target rate goes to zero and the unit state says changeover, so the shift carried a product change as well as production

pipeline.title: Production window
pipeline.text: everything before the target went to zero — the part of the shift that had to make rate

pipeline.title: Rate held
pipeline.text: line throughput against the planned target through that whole window

pipeline.title: Station sweep
pipeline.text: every station on the line, one at a time: rate band, micro-stops, stress, and the condition and quality tags each station type carries

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: target held and no station exception → raise a positive confirmation, not an alarm

inputs.condition: power_charge.vibration_mms vs the other chargers; refinement.purity_pct; inspection.reject_rate_pct; transfer.blocking_time / starvation_time; buffer.buffer_level
inputs.work: work-items on the line and its stations (confidence only)

peers.count: the same station type on the other lines of the same refinery

checks.rule: line_target_rate falls to 0 after running > 0, and unit state is changeover → a planned product change on this line today
mean line_throughput over the production window ≥ hold_pct % of target, and the smooth_min mean never below floor_pct %

no station exception: 15-min mean rate inside ±band_pct of target, no sample below stop_frac × target, ≤ dip_events_max dip episodes, stress < stress_max, and each station type's own condition and quality tags inside band
instability < instab_max, scrap < scrap_max and health > health_min right through the production window
a condition inspection on this line closed today and raised nothing
every planned work item on the line closed inside its own window (planned start + estimated duration, or its due time, whichever is later)
no situation-sourced work item was raised on this line today

ruleOut: a station hiding behind the line average
micro-stops too short to see in the rate
the changeover itself being a fault
work volume as a signal in its own right

confidence.medium: nothing was raised against the line
confidence.high: a condition inspection on the line closed today and nothing was raised against it

references: textbook: busy shift that stayed normal
variant: busy shift that did hide a fault
look-alike: quiet line that looks the same on the headline

refinery.refinement_regulator_sluggish.name: Refinement regulating element responding slowly
refinery.refinement_regulator_sluggish.summary: A Refinement station losing rate against its line target while its control effort climbs to hold the setpoint. Effort up and output down together is a mechanical response problem, not a demand change.

pipeline.title: Expected
pipeline.text: the line target rate — what the station is asked to pass

pipeline.title: Deficit
pipeline.text: target minus the station rate, as a percentage of target

pipeline.title: Effort
pipeline.text: control effort against this station's own first-hour baseline and against the other Refinements

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: behind target · effort climbing · sustained · starving downstream · buffer draining · upstream paced down

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: rate down while effort up → the regulating element, not the demand; recovery after the inspection → high confidence

inputs.work: done INSPECTION work items on this station (confidence only)

checks.rule: rate < target × (1 − deficit_pct/100)
control effort > baseline + effort_rise_pct and rising faster than effort_slope_pct_per_h
behind target for sustain_min

the next station down the line is ≥ starve_per_min behind target at the worst point, and its deficit matches this station's to within starve_match_per_min — the whole shortfall passed straight through
the line buffer drains ≥ buffer_drop_pts while this lasts
the station feeding it paces down too (blocked), and WIP rises ≥ wip_rise_lots
rate recovers ≥ recover_frac of the deficit within recover_within_min of the regulator inspection closing

confidence.high: rate recovered after the regulator was adjusted

refinery.buffer_accumulation.name: Buffer filling from a downstream restriction
refinery.buffer_accumulation.summary: A line buffer taking in more than it lets out for long enough to climb well above its working level, with the inflow unchanged — so the restriction is downstream of the buffer, not a surge upstream.

pipeline.title: Net flow
pipeline.text: inflow minus outflow, sample by sample

pipeline.title: Mass balance
pipeline.text: the level rise the net flow should produce, against the level actually read

pipeline.title: Side
pipeline.text: inflow against its own baseline: unchanged inflow puts the cause on the outflow side

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: accumulating · level high · balance closes · inflow normal · saturation risk · Output behind target

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the station the buffer feeds is the restriction; recovery after it is cleared → high confidence

inputs.work: done INSPECTION work items on the downstream station (confidence only)

checks.rule: in − out > net_per_min for sustain_min
level > first-hour baseline + rise_pts and still rising
integrated net flow ÷ units_per_pct matches the level rise within balance_tol_pct
|median(in over the episode) − median(in over the inflow_local_min before it)| < inflow_band_per_min
saturation risk up by risk_rise and dwell time up by dwell_rise_min
the station the buffer feeds runs ≥ out_deficit_per_min below the line target
level drains ≥ drain_frac of the rise within drain_within_min of the downstream inspection closing

ruleOut: a quality hold inside the buffer

confidence.high: buffer drained after the downstream restriction was cleared

refinery.charger_bearing_wear.name: Power Charge drive bearing wear
refinery.charger_bearing_wear.summary: A Power Charge drive running rougher than the other five chargers and getting worse hour by hour, while its load — rate, charge demand and motor current — has not changed at all.

pipeline.title: Find peers
pipeline.text: the other five Power Charge drives; they run the same duty on the same product

pipeline.title: Expected value
pipeline.text: the peer median vibration plus the steady offset this drive had in the first hour

pipeline.title: Residual
pipeline.text: actual minus expected: roughness the other drives do not have

pipeline.title: Load
pipeline.text: rate, charge demand and motor current against their own baselines — the load has to be unchanged for this to be the machine

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: rougher · climbing · sustained · same load · bearing temperature · energy per unit

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: all required checks → raise; bearing temperature agreeing → medium; an inspection would make it high

inputs.work: INSPECTION work items on this station (confidence only)

peers.count: the other five Power Charge drives

expected.formula: median(peer vibration) + median(own − peer median over baseline_min)

checks.rule: residual > alert_mms
slope(vib, slope_window_min) > min_slope_mms_per_h and the largest 5-min step since onset < max_step_mms
residual > alert_mms for sustain_min
rate and charge demand within load_band_pct, motor current within current_band_pct, of their own baselines
bearing temperature up by temp_rise_c since onset
energy per unit up by energy_rise since onset
a drive inspection on this station has closed

ruleOut: a loose or failing vibration sensor

confidence.medium: bearing temperature or energy per unit agrees

refinery.pressure_transmitter_fault.name: Stabilization pressure transmitter reading wrong
refinery.pressure_transmitter_fault.summary: A Stabilization pressure transmitter jumping around while the local mechanical gauge on the same vessel, the flow meter and the temperature all sit still. The process did not move; the reading did.

pipeline.title: Second tap
pipeline.text: the local mechanical gauge reads the same pressure through a different tap, so the two should track each other

pipeline.title: Offset
pipeline.text: the steady difference between transmitter and gauge over the first hour

pipeline.title: Residual
pipeline.text: transmitter − gauge − offset: pressure only one of the two can see

pipeline.title: Jumpiness
pipeline.text: the largest 5-minute step on each instrument — a connection fault steps, a process swing does not

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: disagrees · steps · gauge steady · flow steady · temperature steady · nothing downstream reacts

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the instrument, not the process; a field check against the gauge → high confidence

inputs.work: done INSTRUMENT_CHECK work items on this station (confidence only)

peers.count: the other five Stabilization stations (sanity check only)

checks.rule: |xmtr − gauge − offset| > res_psi
largest xmtr step inside window_min > step_psi while the gauge's largest step < gauge_step_psi
the gauge's whole range over the episode < gauge_range_psi (it drifts slowly with the vessel, so a fixed morning baseline would not do)
flow meter inside ±flow_band_per_min of its baseline
temperature inside ±temp_band_c of its baseline
control effort inside ±effort_band_pct — the loop did not act on the reading
the next station down the line holds rate within down_band_per_min
the residual settles within settle_min of the instrument check closing

ruleOut: the gauge being the wrong one

confidence.high: confirmed by a field check against the local gauge

refinery.inspection_rejects_upstream.name: Inspection rejects caused upstream at Refinement
refinery.inspection_rejects_upstream.summary: An Inspection gate rejecting several times more than usual while its own calibration and measurement noise stay clean, and the Refinement station feeding it lost purity first. The gate is where it shows, not where it is.

pipeline.title: Gate health
pipeline.text: calibration score, measurement noise and false-reject rate against their own baselines — is the gate itself sound?

pipeline.title: Upstream
pipeline.text: the Refinement station that feeds it on the process_flow layer

pipeline.title: Timing
pipeline.text: when purity left its band against when rejects left theirs; the lead decides which caused which

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: rejects up · gate healthy · purity fell first · quality tags followed · scrap followed · fixed upstream

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the upstream station is the cause; adjusting the gate would only hide it

inputs.work: done QUALITY_CHECK work items on this gate (confidence only)

expected.formula: median(own reject rate over baseline_min), cross-checked against the peer band

checks.rule: reject rate > baseline + rise_pct and > ratio × baseline for sustain_min
over the episode, mean calibration within cal_band, mean measurement noise within noise_band and mean false-reject rate within false_band of the same tag's median over the gate_local_min before it
the feeding Refinement's purity falls purity_drop_pct below baseline, and starts between min_lead_min and max_lead_min before the rejects do
the same Refinement's defect rate, yield and consistency move with the purity
first-pass yield falls fpy_drop_pct and line scrap rises scrap_rise — the rejects are real product
rejects fall back ≥ recover_frac within recover_within_min of the upstream adjustment

ruleOut: the gate being set too tight

confidence.high: an independent quality check confirmed the rejects, and they fell after the upstream adjustment

refinery.gross_vs_effective_output.name: Gross rate above sustainable downstream capacity
refinery.gross_vs_effective_output.summary: A Power Charge station pushed above the rate the next station can actually sustain. The headline number looks healthy, but the difference goes into work in process, blocking time and defects instead of out of the Output door.

pipeline.title: Window
pipeline.text: a rolling hour — long enough for the difference between gross and shipped to add up to something the counters can see through their own noise

pipeline.title: Gross against shipped
pipeline.text: this station's rate minus the line Output's, with the fixed counter bias between the pair removed, added up over the window

pipeline.title: Where it went
pipeline.text: the WIP the line gained over the same window — the extra product has to be somewhere

pipeline.title: Mass balance
pipeline.text: cumulative gross-minus-shipped against the WIP curve, point by point

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: made more than it shipped · WIP absorbing · Output no better and no worse · balance closes · downstream capped · defects up · demand cut

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the gross rate is a number, not product; cut the demand to the sustainable rate

peers.count: the other five Power Charge stations (sanity check only)

expected.formula: downstream 30-min mean rate + the pair's own gap over baseline_min

checks.rule: Σ(rate − line Output rate − the pair's counter bias) × step over the window > gap_units
line WIP gained ≥ wip_rise_lots across the window
mean Output rate ≤ its own baseline + out_gain_per_min and never below baseline − out_floor_per_min — the extra never left the line, and nothing collapsed either
cumulative (gross − shipped) correlates with the WIP curve at r > balance_r
Transfer blocking time up by block_rise
downstream defect and rework rates up by defect_rise, line scrap up by scrap_rise
the gap closes by ≥ cut_frac after the demand is reduced, and WIP drains

ruleOut: a quality problem making the extra product
a counting error between the two stations

confidence.high: the gap closed and WIP drained after the demand was cut

references: textbook: over-pacing into a capped line
variant: over-pacing with a buffer to absorb it

refinery.charger_fault_cascade.name: Power Charge interruption cascading down the line
refinery.charger_fault_cascade.summary: A Power Charge station whose output collapses to idle for one sample, taking the stations after it down in flow order within the same five minutes and blocking the one before it. The order of events is what names the origin.

pipeline.title: Collapse
pipeline.text: the station's rate against its own hour-before baseline, and its motor current against idle

pipeline.title: Spread
pipeline.text: every station downstream on the process_flow layer, in order, in the same sample

pipeline.title: Attenuation
pipeline.text: the deficit should shrink with distance: material already past the charger keeps moving

pipeline.title: Upstream
pipeline.text: the feeding station drops too, but it is blocked, not stopped — and material availability is normal

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: collapse · drive at idle · downstream in order · attenuating · upstream blocked · recovery

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the first station to fall, with its drive at idle, is the origin; everything after it is consequence

inputs.up: sources[process_flow] throughput_per_min and the line head's material_availability
inputs.work: done MAINTENANCE work items on this station (confidence only)

peers.count: the other five Power Charge stations (sanity check only)

expected.formula: median(rate over the hour before the sample)

checks.rule: rate < collapse_frac × its own hour-before baseline
motor current < idle_frac × its baseline in the same sample
every station downstream is below down_frac of its baseline in the same sample
the deficit shrinks with distance downstream
the next sample is back above recover_frac of baseline — an interruption, not a stop
the feeding station is above up_frac × idle (blocked, not stopped) and line-head material availability > avail_pct
Transfer starvation time up by starve_rise in the same sample, then blocking time up in the next
a maintenance item on this station closed and no further collapse followed

confidence.high: the source fault was repaired and nothing recurred

references: variant: supply loss at the head of the line

refinery.manual_overcorrection.name: Manual corrections amplifying a charge-rate oscillation
refinery.manual_overcorrection.summary: A charge rate swinging further each cycle while the controller output moves against it, one sample out of phase. Each correction lands before the last one has settled, so the correcting is what grows the swing.

pipeline.title: Baseline
pipeline.text: the charge rate the station held for the hour before the swings started, and the mid-point of the swing itself (the median through the episode)

pipeline.title: Cycles
pipeline.text: turning points either side of that mid-point, and the peak-to-peak of each cycle

pipeline.title: Growth
pipeline.text: later cycles against earlier ones — a disturbance decays, a correction loop grows

pipeline.title: Phase
pipeline.text: correlation between charge rate and controller output over the episode: pushing against the response instead of with it

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: swinging · growing · anti-phase · oscillation index · still running · damped after

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the control action, not the process; go back to the validated setting

peers.count: the other five Power Charge stations

expected.formula: median(charge_rate over baseline_min before the first turning point)

checks.rule: at least min_turns turning points alternating about the mid-point of the episode, with ≥ 2 cycles of min_pp_pct peak-to-peak
the largest cycle ≥ growth_ratio × the first cycle
corr(charge, controller output) < phase_r over the episode
oscillation index > osc_min for osc_sustain_min
rate never below running_frac × baseline — the station kept running, so this is not a trip
throughput and the downstream station swing with it, and line instability rises
the charge rate settles inside settle_pct of baseline for settle_min

confidence.medium: throughput and instability moved with it
confidence.high: the swing damped as soon as the corrections stopped

refinery.transfer_hard_block.name: Transfer gate physically blocked
refinery.transfer_hard_block.summary: A Transfer gate at zero rate for several samples with its motor current spiking at the moment it stopped and then sitting at idle. A current spike into a hard stop is an obstruction, not a control problem.

pipeline.title: Stop
pipeline.text: gate rate at zero for more than one sample — not a dip, a stop

pipeline.title: Spike
pipeline.text: motor current in the sample it stopped, against its running baseline

pipeline.title: Idle
pipeline.text: motor current through the stop: the drive is turning against nothing, or not turning

pipeline.title: Hold
pipeline.text: the rest of the line at zero too — a controlled hold rather than one station failing quietly

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: zero · current spike · idle through · line held · restart surge · availability

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: a physical obstruction; hold, confirm, clear with the validated procedure

inputs.others: the other stations on the line: throughput_per_min
inputs.work: done PROCEDURE work items on this gate (confidence only)

peers.count: the other five Transfer gates (sanity check only)

expected.formula: median(transfer_rate_per_min over baseline_min before the stop)

checks.rule: gate rate < zero_per_min for ≥ min_stop_min
motor current in the stopping sample > spike_ratio × its running baseline
motor current < idle_frac × baseline for the rest of the stop
every other station on the line is below hold_frac × its baseline during the stop
motor current > restart_ratio × baseline on the first moving sample, and the rate comes back in steps
gate stress up by stress_rise and starvation only at the restart
a block-clearing procedure closed on this gate and the gate has run normally since

confidence.medium: the restart surge or the stress trace agrees
confidence.high: confirmed visually and cleared by the validated procedure

refinery.charger_micro_stops.name: Recurring Power Charge micro-stops
refinery.charger_micro_stops.summary: A Power Charge station taking repeated short interruptions that each recover on their own. No single one is worth stopping for; together they are costing a measurable share of the line's output.

pipeline.title: Baseline
pipeline.text: the median rate this station held over the two hours before the window — a local baseline, because the line pace drifts slowly all day

pipeline.title: Events
pipeline.text: samples more than dip_frac below that baseline inside a rolling hour — recurrence, not one event

pipeline.title: Short
pipeline.text: each run of them is brief and the rate returns to baseline on its own; the station never goes near zero

pipeline.title: Cost
pipeline.text: the mean shortfall across the whole stretch, as a share of baseline

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: recurring · self-recovering · never stopped · real loss · downstream starved · supply normal · demand peaks

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: the accumulation is the finding; inspect at the next pause rather than stopping now

inputs.head: line head: material_availability, supply_variability
inputs.work: open INSPECTION work items on this station (confidence only)

peers.count: the other five Power Charge stations

expected.formula: median(rate over the baseline_min before the window)

checks.rule: ≥ min_events samples below (1 − dip_frac) × the local baseline inside window_min, in ≥ min_runs separate runs — recurrence, not one block of reduced rate
every run of them ≤ max_episode_min, and the samples between the runs average ≥ recover_frac × baseline — the station is back at full rate in between
rate never below stop_frac × baseline and motor current never at idle — not a block or a trip
mean shortfall from the first event to now ≥ loss_pct of baseline
Transfer starvation time rises with the dips by starve_rise, while blocking time does not
line-head material availability stays above avail_pct — not a supply problem
charge demand and oscillation index are higher in the dip samples than between them
an inspection on this station has closed

ruleOut: a counting problem at this station

confidence.high: confirmed by an inspection of the station

references: variant: one long stop of the same size

refinery.purity_drift_to_limit.name: Refinement purity drifting toward the spec limit
refinery.purity_drift_to_limit.summary: A Refinement station whose purity has been falling steadily since the input characteristic shifted and stayed shifted. Still in specification, but the margin is narrowing and the direction is the finding.

pipeline.title: Input
pipeline.text: the input characteristic index against its own baseline: a shift that persists, not a batch

pipeline.title: Drift
pipeline.text: purity slope over the last hour, and how far it has gone from its baseline

pipeline.title: Margin
pipeline.text: purity against the specification limit, and the time left at the current slope

pipeline.title: Compensation
pipeline.text: control effort: whether the loop is holding the purity or has given up ground

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: falling · persistent input shift · margin narrowing · time to limit · rejects following · corrected

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: an input shift the current setting no longer covers; adjust before the margin goes

expected.model: own baseline and the spec limit

checks.rule: purity below its baseline by drop_pct and falling faster than min_slope_pct_per_h
input characteristic index above its baseline by input_rise for input_sustain_min and still there
purity − spec_limit_pct < margin_pct
the other Refinements are not drifting with it (peer median within peer_margin_pct of its baseline)
downstream reject rate rises reject_rise_pct about reject_lag_min later
control effort stepped up to compensate
purity recovers ≥ recover_frac within recover_within_min of the control effort step

ruleOut: measurement drift on the purity analyser
a single off-spec lot of input

confidence.high: the trend reversed after a validated adjustment

references: textbook: input shift, corrected in time

refinery.changeover_schedule_risk.name: Changeover prerequisites against the clock
refinery.changeover_schedule_risk.summary: A planned product changeover whose cross-team prerequisites were still open with less time left than they need back-to-back. Arithmetic on the plan, not a diagnosis — and the answer was to run them in parallel.

pipeline.title: Plan
pipeline.text: the open planned changeover on this line and the time it is due

pipeline.title: Prerequisites
pipeline.text: the material-staging and quality-release tasks it depends on, and their typical durations

pipeline.title: Arithmetic
pipeline.text: request lead plus the remaining prerequisites run back-to-back, against the time left

pipeline.title: Where it stands now
pipeline.text: what has since closed, and whether the line has actually started its run-down

pipeline.title: Checks
pipeline.text: changeover due · prerequisites open · no slack left · parallel instead · now clear · running long

pipeline.title: Conclusion
pipeline.text: a coordination decision with a deadline, not an equipment finding

inputs.work: work-items on this line: the open CHANGEOVER item, its dependencies, and the MATERIAL_STAGE and QUALITY_RELEASE items with their estimatedDurationMinutes

expected.formula: now + request_lead_min + Σ(estimatedDurationMinutes of the open prerequisites) against the changeover due time
expected.fitOn: the work list's own planned durations

checks.rule: an open planned CHANGEOVER item on this line, due within lead_min
at least one of its MATERIAL_STAGE / QUALITY_RELEASE prerequisites is still incomplete at this time
request_lead_min + Σ(remaining prerequisite durations) ≥ time left to the changeover due time + slack_min
the prerequisites were worked overlapping rather than back-to-back
every prerequisite and every declared dependency is now done
the line target has gone to 0, the state reads changeover, and the stations are running down upstream first

ruleOut: an equipment problem on the line
the changeover being started too early

confidence.n/a: a schedule clash worked out from the plan, not a diagnosis

references: look-alike: prerequisites late but the changeover not due yet

conclusion.label: Cause
conclusion.text: Nothing wrong with F4: a heavy planned slate, worked on schedule, on a line that held 99.8 % of plan with every station inside its band
conclusion.confidenceText: Confirmed by a full station sweep and a clean inspection on the line

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: F4 and each of its 5 stations against the 120/min target, up to the 13:50 changeover. The band is ±4 % of target; no station left it.

checks.label: A planned changeover on top of a full shift
checks.value: F4 is on Product A → Product C; its target rate went from 120/min to 0 at 13:50 and the line state reads changeover. 6 planned jobs sit on this line today, 5 of them closed.
checks.why: A changeover is the busiest thing a line does short of a breakdown: product switch, material, quality release, and the run-down itself. It is planned work, not a fault.

checks.label: Held its target right up to the changeover
checks.value: 119.7/min average against a 120/min target (99.8 % of plan) over 5 h 45 min, with the 30-minute mean never below 99.2 % of target (floor 97 %).
checks.why: A line that is genuinely in trouble gives rate away first. Holding plan for a whole shift is the single strongest evidence that nothing upstream of Output was limiting.

checks.label: All 5 stations swept, no exception
checks.value: Bulk Intake 118.0–122.9/min, input quality 97.7–98.5; Power Charge 118.5–121.2/min, vibration 2.47–3.00 mm/s; Shaping 118.2–122.5/min; Transfer 118.1–122.3/min, blocked 0.62 max, starved 0.56 max; Output 118.2–121.2/min, on-time 96.0–97.6 %. Every 30-min mean inside ±4 % of target; no sample below 90 %; no station with more than 2 dips; peak stress 19.3 of 30.
checks.why: The line average can hide one slow station: upstream blocks and downstream starves, and the Output rate still looks fine for a while. The sweep is what rules that out.

checks.label: Line KPIs flat all shift
checks.value: Instability 0.97–1.05 (normal is about 1), scrap 0.77 % at worst, health never below 99.3 %.
checks.why: Instability, scrap and health pick up oscillation, stops and quality losses that a rate band would miss. All three sat still.

checks.label: A condition inspection on the line came back clean
checks.value: Power Charge inspection (wk-002, F4 · Power Charge) closed 09:36 — and nothing was raised off the back of it.
checks.why: Somebody was at the machine today and wrote nothing up. That is a different kind of evidence from a trend, and it is what makes this a confirmation rather than an absence of alarms.

checks.label: Planned work closed inside its window
checks.value: Routine quality sample 08:45+10 min, done 08:49; Power Charge inspection 09:30+15 min, done 09:36; Production huddle 10:00+10 min, done 10:06; Stage Grade B material 13:10+40 min, done 13:52; Release Grade B 13:10+20 min, done 13:31. Stage Grade B material ran 2 min over.
checks.why: Workload is only a problem when tasks start colliding. These were worked one after another, each inside its own window.

checks.label: Nothing raised against the line
checks.value: No condition- or situation-driven work item exists on this line today.
checks.why: Every other line with a problem today has a job on it that the problem created. This one has none.

checks.value: 50.7 → 58.3 (+7.6) since 12:05, and still 58.3 now — 2 h at the new level. Alert level is +4 for 30 min.
checks.why: This is the cause, and it is measured upstream of the purity. A shift that persists is a different feed, not a batch; the setting that was right this morning is no longer enough for it.

checks.why: Operators need the time, not the number. Half an hour of margin is a decision; two hours is a note for the next shift.

checks.label: The loop was asked for more

checks.why: A step that is held is a deliberate adjustment, not the loop hunting. It is also the thing that turned the purity around.

checks.why: The input did not come back; the purity did. That is what tells you the setting, not the feed, was what needed changing.

ruledOut.cause: Measurement drift on the purity analyser
ruledOut.reason: Two independent signals moved with it: the input characteristic index (+7.6) before, and Inspection's reject rate (2.21 → 2.93 %) after. An analyser drifting on its own moves neither.

ruledOut.cause: A single off-spec lot of input
ruledOut.reason: The input characteristic has stayed at 58.3 for 2 h — it is the new normal, not a lot passing through. A single lot would have cleared the station in minutes.
